profile.name: Itsuki Kawamura
profile.title: Cloud Infrastructure Engineer
profile.summary: Cloud Infrastructure Engineer with hands-on AWS migration and server build experience, followed by large-scale multi-cloud audit, governance and operations across AWS, Azure and Google Cloud. Has authored CloudFormation templates and a VBA reporting automation in professional work. A networking and hybrid connectivity foundation helps diagnose cloud connectivity; Terraform and CI/CD project work extends this cloud infrastructure base.

projects.name: AWS Windows Maintenance Automation
projects.summary: Automated maintenance workflow for a private Windows Server EC2 instance using AWS managed services.
implementation: EC2 has no public IP.
Administrative access uses AWS Systems Manager instead of RDP from the Internet.
Step Functions orchestrates stop, snapshot, start, patching, reboot, health checks and notifications.
EventBridge Scheduler triggers monthly maintenance.
Lambda performs patch scanning and starts the maintenance workflow when missing patches are detected.
Infrastructure is deployed with Terraform.
GitHub Actions uses AWS OIDC for CI/CD.
A manual destroy workflow is included.
validation: Successfully tested the normal maintenance workflow.
Tested failure handling by intentionally using an invalid Windows service name.
Confirmed automatic EventBridge Scheduler to Step Functions execution.

projects.name: AWS Terraform CI/CD with GitHub OIDC
projects.summary: Terraform CI/CD pipeline using GitHub Actions and AWS OIDC without long-lived AWS access keys.
implementation: GitHub Actions authenticates to AWS using OIDC.
Terraform runs format, initialization, validation, plan and apply stages.
Terraform state is stored remotely in S3.
S3 versioning is enabled for the state bucket.
Terraform S3 native state locking is used.
The AWS trust policy restricts GitHub OIDC subject claims.
lessons_learned: GitHub-hosted runners are ephemeral, so local Terraform state cannot be relied on across workflow runs.
Remote Terraform state is required for repeatable CI/CD deployments.
Recent GitHub repositories may use immutable repository identifiers in OIDC subject claims.

GitHub Actions, Ansible and Docker are evidenced by personal projects; Kubernetes remains learning.

Do not claim ownership of the entire AWS migration architecture: a senior engineer designed the overall architecture. The candidate adapted existing patterns, designed and configured routing for assigned systems, and tested backup connectivity.

Project dates below overlap because some assignments ran alongside wider operations work; do not add their durations together as if they were sequential.
If a recruiter asks for an unrecorded metric, certification, project detail, or exact responsibility, say the information is not available rather than guessing.
A repository README can support a project claim only when its actual content has been retrieved and provided to the assistant.
Treat all entries in projects as personal portfolio projects, not employment. Respect each project status and validation notes.
AWS Organizations, OU, SCP, IAM role deployment and Lucidscale are described in the earlier portfolio context; avoid giving project-level ownership details beyond those recorded there.

Do not claim the candidate designed or authored AWS SCPs or the Prisma Cloud IAM-role StackSet. Those controls predated their involvement; their contribution was OU placement, exception handling and policy-related troubleshooting.
When describing the scale of the audit estate, distinguish the thousands/hundreds/dozens of environments in scope from the subset personally onboarded or handled.
The incorrect BGP AS-number troubleshooting episode belongs to the CAC AWS migration assignment, not the earlier Kintetsu migration.
For the CAC AS-number incident, the candidate compared design documents and reported the discrepancy; they did not change provider-managed equipment.

CloudFormation professional ownership covers candidate-authored VPC, Route Tables, Security Groups, ALB and CloudFront templates. Do not infer that EC2 or other compute in the same project was managed with those templates.

For the website OS upgrade project, do not claim completed production migration, application validation or final infrastructure testing. The candidate delivered new servers and a test plan, then left before subsequent stages.
For AWS SAA, state only that the candidate passed the exam. Do not describe it as a currently active certification or make claims about current validity.

For broad recruiter questions about strengths or fit, lead with cloud infrastructure, AWS migration and multi-cloud operations. Explain network experience as a differentiator for cloud connectivity, not the candidate’s desired primary on-premises role.
The candidate prefers remote-friendly cloud-focused roles, but has not specified a remote-only requirement or a precise onsite schedule. Do not invent one.

Never end an answer with a generic referral such as “see the full portfolio for details”. The context already contains specific work and project examples; use a relevant example in the answer instead.

recruiter_faq.question: Is Itsuki only a network engineer?
recruiter_faq.answer: No. The career target is cloud infrastructure and operations. Itsuki built AWS environments and servers, authored CloudFormation templates, and later worked in large-scale multi-cloud audit and governance. Earlier L2/L3 and hybrid network work adds depth for cloud connectivity and troubleshooting.

recruiter_faq.question: Has Itsuki used Terraform in production?
recruiter_faq.answer: Yes, in a bounded support and onboarding role: reviewed and tested Prisma Cloud-generated Terraform for customer cloud integration, corrected provider version settings when needed, prepared instructions, and troubleshot customer execution. Customers normally ran it. Independently authored Terraform infrastructure and CI/CD work is shown in personal portfolio projects, not claimed as equivalent production ownership.

recruiter_faq.question: Is Itsuki a DevOps or Kubernetes specialist?
recruiter_faq.answer: The professional base is infrastructure, networking and cloud operations. CI/CD, containers and Kubernetes are areas of development; specialist production experience is not established here.

recruiter_faq.question: What kind of security experience does Itsuki have?
recruiter_faq.answer: Cloud posture and governance operations across AWS, Azure and Google Cloud: Prisma Cloud onboarding, permission troubleshooting, and alert investigation. Examples include password-policy findings, missing application access, default VPCs and overly broad routing. The candidate checked the actual resource and cited resource IDs when explaining unresolved findings. Dedicated SOC or SIEM response is not claimed.

recruiter_faq.question: Has Itsuki automated a professional workflow?
recruiter_faq.answer: Yes. The candidate built an Excel VBA macro that reconciled Prisma Cloud alert-status exports with an account register and generated approximately 20 company-specific monthly reports. The process took about 1–2 person-days including checks. The pre-automation time was not measured, so no quantified saving is claimed.

recruiter_faq.question: What is Itsuki’s main professional strength?
recruiter_faq.answer: The main strength is cloud infrastructure delivery and operations, supported by hybrid networking expertise. In a CAC AWS migration, the candidate built about 20 application/database servers across five environments and traced a failed initial connection to an AS-number discrepancy in network design documents. In a later multi-cloud audit assignment, the candidate supported Prisma Cloud onboarding at large estate scale and built a VBA workflow to generate about 20 company reports monthly. Independently authored Terraform/CI/CD work is represented as personal projects.
